summary: Builds a frequency distribution from one scalar attribute component. It outputs a fixed number of bin points with a count attribute, optional bin value attribute, and controls for quantization and out-of-range values.

key_params.name: attrclass
key_params.note: Point, vertex, or primitive class to sample

key_params.name: inputattrscope
key_params.note: Scalar attribute or vector component to histogram

key_params.name: useinputrange
key_params.note: Use an explicit input value range

key_params.name: inputrangemin
key_params.note: Minimum input value for explicit range

key_params.name: inputrangemax
key_params.note: Maximum input value for explicit range

key_params.name: outsiderange
key_params.note: Clamp, discard, or add extra out-of-range bins

key_concepts: Histogram POP samples one scalar attribute component and outputs a frequency distribution as POP points.
The output contains one point per bin, with Count tracking how many input values landed in each interval.
Input Range defines the min/max span divided into Number of Bins; out-of-range values can be clamped, discarded, or counted in extra bins.
Output Bin Value can write a separate BinValue-style attribute for the interval start/value of each bin.
Vector attributes must be reduced or scoped to one component, such as P(1), before histogramming.
The result is analysis geometry rather than annotated source geometry, and is often viewed through POP to CHOP or a POP viewer graph.
common_gotchas: Histogram operates on a single component, so reduce vector attributes with Math POP or scope a component like P(1).
The output is bins as POP points, not the original geometry with annotations.
Out-of-range handling changes totals; use extra bins when preserving discarded counts matters.
